title: Consciousness diagnostics of subacute and chronic patients using pupillometry
summary: The diagnosis of disorders of consciousness remains challenging due to the risk of misdiagnosis. This study investigates whether pupillometry can serve as a suitable diagnostic tool to assess patients state of consciousness.

criteria:
Inclusion criteria:
Good german language skills, date of brain injury at least 21 days ago, patients with a UWS, MCS, MCS+, or EMCS diagnosis based on the CRS-R scale and, if applicable, SECONDs scale, informed consent from the patient or authorized representative
Exclusion criteria:
Invasive mechanical ventilation, strong central sedation medication through long-acting sedatives/benzodiazepines/opioids, acute epileptic seizure, eye disease with surgery on both sides, patients in EMCS and with proven aphasia
